assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into controllable artificial atoms strongly coupled to single microwave photons, giving dispersive qubit readout, the transmon-era architecture and a general platform for quantum optics on a chip. It is original, conceptually clear and underpins most of today's superconducting quantum processors. I recognise this is my own field, so I weigh it against the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which is related but a distinct discovery.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 Blais-Huang-Wallraff-Girvin-Schoelkopf proposal and the Yale experiments by Schoelkopf's group are the decisive core; Blais and Girvin supplied the theory and Schoelkopf the experimental realisation. Wallraff (strong-coupling experiment) and Devoret, already honoured in 2025, also contributed, so a three-person configuration from this list is defensible but leaves credit pressure on Wallraff, who is not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Strong coupling was confirmed independently by many groups over two decades, with direct engineering consequences in multi-qubit devices. Recognition now is timely, though a committee may worry about following 2025 with another superconducting-circuit award so soon.
uncertainties: Whether recognising circuit QED so soon after the 2025 circuit prize is balanced across physics.
Wallraff's role, and the 2004 theory/experiment split, are not covered by the supplied credited names.
I have a field and institutional proximity bias (Chalmers/WACQT) that I cannot fully correct for.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposals for quantum gates with trapped ions and, with colleagues, for atom-based quantum simulation, provided the first concrete blueprint for scalable quantum computation and shaped the experimental programmes of ion and neutral-atom platforms. The impact on quantum technology is deep, original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair is clean and compact: the 1995 trapped-ion gate proposal is jointly theirs, and both led later work on quantum simulation and quantum networks. This is a natural two-person theory prize, though experimental realisation (Wineland, already recognised in 2012; Blatt, Monroe, Wineland groups) is partly recognised elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Experimental realisation of ion gates and neutral-atom simulation is extensively confirmed and now mature. Timing is good given the 2025 and 2012 prizes in adjacent areas.
uncertainties: Overlap in subject matter with the Wineland 2012 prize and with other quantum-simulation candidates.
Zoller also appears in other candidates, so allocation of one scientist across prizes needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, delivered the best clocks ever built, with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, and opens redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The idea is original and the impact is demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated it with strontium; Ye's group pushed it to record precision and many-body clock physics. The two-name configuration is coherent. John Hall's 2005 prize covered related frequency-comb work, which I treat as separate.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce clock performance, and the international metrology community is preparing a redefinition of the second. This is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is seen as physics discovery or metrology instrumentation.
Credit for ion-clock and comb precursors (Hall/Hansch 2005) overlaps conceptually; Ludlow and Hinkley et al. are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observing the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and fermionic Hubbard physics in optical lattices established cold atoms as clean quantum simulators of strongly correlated matter. The work is conceptually clear and widely used, though simulation of the full Hubbard model remains incomplete.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch realised the bosonic Mott transition (Nature 2002); Esslinger led fermionic Mott and related experiments. Zoller (with Jaksch) gave the key theory but I would rather reserve him for B014 to avoid double-counting; hence an experimental trio.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many labs and now a standard platform, though high-impact answers about, for example, d-wave pairing in the Hubbard model are still pending. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether theory credit (Jaksch, Zoller) should be included.
Hubbard-model quantum simulation has not yet resolved its flagship problems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator opened the field of time-reversal-invariant topological phases and influenced Majorana and quantum-device thinking, including superconducting hybrid circuits. It is original and strongly conceptual.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the Z2 invariants and quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group made the HgTe observation following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's prediction. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu are omitted from the supplied credit, which complicates a fair prize, but the proposed three are individually decisive.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by ARPES, transport and many material platforms, and Nobel-level recognition is widely expected. Not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore is not in the supplied names.
Practical device impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links quantum foundations to secure communication; BB84 and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol are original, lucid and have driven an entire subfield including satellite and fibre networks. Following the 2022 Bell-test prize, recognition is thematically coherent.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard created BB84; Ekert proposed the E91 protocol using Bell inequalities. The trio is the natural configuration, with the caveat that security-proof and experimental developments involve many others.
assessment.maturity: Commercial and field deployments exist, but practical security rests on implementations that are still scrutinised, and the question is partly information science rather than physics.
uncertainties: Fit with the physics prize, given the mix of computer science and cryptography.
Implementation security and the long-term role of post-quantum cryptography.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle theory of twisted bilayer graphene and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity launched moire quantum matter, a very active and conceptually surprising field. Its originality is high and growth has been rapid.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. The three names make a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration; Cao and others are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states remains debated, so the interpretation is not yet fully stable. Somewhat early.
uncertainties: The superconducting mechanism and sample dependence are unresolved.
Junior co-authors such as Yuan Cao are outside the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics enabled ground-state cooling, quantum control of mechanical oscillators and quantum-limited measurement, and links to microwave-optical transduction and superconducting circuits that are relevant to quantum technology. The topic is original and broadly useful, but it includes several loosely related achievements.
assessment.attribution: Kippenberg and Vahala demonstrated radiation-pressure coupling in microresonators, and Aspelmeyer led quantum-regime experiments; Teufel, Lehnert and Painter, who achieved ground-state cooling in superconducting and nanomechanical systems, are not in the supplied credit, so the credit is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Quantum ground-state control is firmly established, but the field is a compound of several discoveries and the leading applications, such as LIGO-style sensing, rely on prior work.
uncertainties: Credit for Teufel, Lehnert, Painter, Marquardt and others is missing from the supplied names.
The discovery is compound and the single flagship claim is unclear.
